sources.what: Source of api.nasa.gov, the key gateway/docs for NASA open APIs (APOD, NeoWs, DONKI, EPIC, Mars photos, etc.).

sources.note: https://api.nasa.gov/{planetary/apod,neo/rest/v1,DONKI/*,EPIC/api} · free api.data.gov key (DEMO_KEY allowed) · regular key 1,000 req/h; DEMO_KEY 30 req/h & 50 req/day per IP (api.data.gov developer manual) · terms: README says NASA only proxies third-party endpoints (see each original provider); image copyright/commercial terms not stated on page (APOD images are often third-party copyrighted: check per-image credit). images-api.nasa.gov (NASA Image & Video Library) needs no key.

sources.what: Official open-source service behind the APOD endpoint (Astronomy Picture of the Day, 1995-present).
sources.use: Look up the APOD for a case date (e.g., 2004-11-14 Nimitz) as a period-appropriate sky 'postcard'; can be self-hosted.
sources.note: https://api.nasa.gov/planetary/apod?date=YYYY-MM-DD&api_key=… · same api.data.gov key/limits as above · code Apache-2.0; RESTRICTIVE: many APOD images are copyrighted by their photographers (the 'copyright' field is returned); use only public-domain ones or link out.

sources.what: Official tutorials/FAQs for The Space Devs APIs: Launch Library 2 (every orbital/suborbital launch, historical + upcoming).
sources.use: 'Was it a rocket launch?' deduction: check launches (with pad lat/lon and time) near an incident; Vandenberg/Cape plumes are classic UFO reports.
sources.note: https://ll.thespacedevs.com/2.3.0/ (lldev.thespacedevs.com for dev) · no auth for free tier · free: 15 non-authenticated req/h; higher via Patreon-supported keys · commercial-use/attribution terms not stated on the API page ('accessible to everyone, for free'). Cache heavily.

sources.what: Python client for the Space-Track.org REST API (official USSF TLE/GP/SATCAT/decay history).
sources.use: Build-time script to pull historical TLEs for a date (e.g., Starlink trains, rocket-body reentries) to feed satellite.js in the night-sky 'was it a satellite?' view.
sources.note: https://www.space-track.org/basicspacedata/query/… · free account login (no sharing credentials) · 30 req/min, 300 req/h · RESTRICTIVE: user agreement forbids transferring data 'to any other entity without prior express approval', except basic SSA data (TLEs/OMMs/SATCAT/decay) which may be redistributed with attribution; server-side only. Alternative for current elements: CelesTrak GP https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/gp.php?GROUP=…&FORMAT=json (no auth; data updates every 2 h, download at most once per update, >100 MB/day may be firewalled; HTTP 403 when repeating before an update).

sources.what: Python wrapper for the N2YO REST API (satellite positions, visual passes, 'what's up' above a location).
sources.use: Heavens-Above-style 'visible passes' and 'what was overhead' lookups for a live 'report a sighting' mini-tool.
sources.note: https://api.n2yo.com/rest/v1/satellite/ · free key after registration (apiKey query param) · per hour: TLE 1,000, positions 1,000, visualpasses 100, radiopasses 100, above 100 · commercial use: 'free but transaction limited'; multiple keys to evade limits may get you blocked; attribution not stated. Key must stay server-side (Vercel function). Wrapper is small/old (last push 2024).

sources.what: Astropy-affiliated Python package for online astronomy services, including JPL Horizons and JPL SBDB/SSD APIs.

sources.what: Community guide/notebooks to NOAA NCEI's climate data APIs (CDO v2 and Access Data Service).
sources.use: Historic daily weather (temps, precipitation, cloud cover) for 1940s-90s cases where IEM METAR coverage is thin.
sources.note: CDO v2: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/cdo-web/api/v2/ · free token (header 'token') · 5 req/s and 10,000 req/day per token; date range max 1 year (10 years for monthly/annual) · Access Data Service: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/services/data/v1 (no auth mentioned, limits not stated) · terms not stated (NOAA data). Guide last updated 2023.

sources.what: MCP server wrapping the NOAA AviationWeather.gov Data API (METAR, TAF, PIREP, SIGMET).
sources.use: Live 'tonight's conditions' widget and recent PIREPs for the companion site; also shows the API shape for a Next.js route.
sources.note: https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/{metar,taf,pirep,…} · no auth, custom User-Agent recommended · 100 req/min; max 400 entries/response; only previous 30 days (use IEM for history); NO CORS, so proxy through Vercel · terms: 'keep requests limited in scope and frequency'; use cache files for bulk.

sources.what: Tool that parses the FAA Releasable Aircraft Database (US civil registry) daily.
sources.use: Resolve N-numbers seen in ADS-B tracks near a sighting to aircraft type/owner for the 'it was a plane' reveal.
sources.note: https://registry.faa.gov/database/ReleasableAircraft.zip (CSV bundle, ~60 MB, refreshed daily 11:30 pm CT) · no auth · no API; bulk download only · terms not stated in sources we could reach (faa.gov page returned 403); contains owner PII, so show type data and avoid displaying owners · repo has no license.

sources.what: APIs.guru: machine-readable OpenAPI directory of thousands of public APIs.
sources.use: Generate typed clients (openapi-typescript) for gov/space APIs that publish specs, and discover more data sources.
sources.note: https://api.apis.guru/v2/list.json · no auth · limits not stated · definitions CC0 (author-contributed) or fair use (collected from public sources); prefer REST API over raw GitHub links.

sources.what: GSA's shared API-key/proxy service; confirmed users in this list: NASA (api.nasa.gov), govinfo, Congress.gov.
sources.use: One signup key for most US-government APIs in this list; documents limits and header usage.
sources.note: https://api.data.gov/ (signup + developer manual) · key via X-Api-Key header, api_key param or basic auth · default 1,000 req/h per key; DEMO_KEY 30 req/h and 50 req/day per IP; individual agencies may set higher (govinfo 36k/h) or lower · repo NOASSERTION license.

sources.what: Official TypeScript SDK for the Claude API (Messages, streaming, tool use, batches, prompt caching).
sources.use: Server-side NPC dialogue/interrogation, hint generation and content tooling from Next.js route handlers; cache the case-file system prompt to cut cost.
sources.note: Auth: x-api-key (server only). Pricing (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing): Claude Haiku 4.5 $1/$5 per MTok in/out, Claude Sonnet 5 $2/$10; Batch API 50% off; cache hits 0.1x input; FAQ: 'New users receive a small amount of free credits'. Limits (platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits): Start tier 1,000 RPM / 2,000,000 ITPM / 400,000 OTPM for Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5; monthly spend cap $500 (Start), $1,000 (Build); cached reads don't count toward ITPM. Terms (anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms): 'Customer...owns its Outputs'; 'Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services'. Already in catalog: vercel/ai can wrap it.

sources.what: Claude Agent SDK (TypeScript) - agent loop with tools/MCP/subagents built on Claude Code; repo has no LICENSE file.
sources.use: Offline content pipeline: agents that draft/verify case files, cross-check clue consistency, batch-generate NPC lore; not for per-request game runtime.
sources.note: Auth: Anthropic API key (or Bedrock/Vertex). Billed at Claude API token rates (see anthropic-sdk-typescript). LICENCE FLAG: GitHub reports no licence; README says use is governed by Anthropic Commercial Terms of Service - proprietary terms, not OSS. Rate limits: same org limits as Claude API.

sources.what: Official JS/TS SDK for the OpenAI API (Responses, Realtime, Audio/TTS, Images).
sources.use: Alternative/fallback NPC LLM, gpt-realtime voice interviews, tts-1 narration for radio-chatter clips.
sources.note: Auth: Bearer API key. Pricing (developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing): gpt-5-nano $0.05 in / $0.40 out per 1M tokens; tts-1 $15.00 / 1M characters, tts-1-hd $30.00 / 1M chars; gpt-realtime-mini audio $10 in / $20 out per 1M tokens. Free tier: not stated. Rate limits: not read (tier-based). Output-ownership terms: openai.com policy pages returned 403 - not verified.

sources.what: Official Google Gen AI SDK for TypeScript/JS (Gemini API and Vertex AI).
sources.use: Cheap bulk NPC chatter / hint rephrasing on Flash-Lite; multimodal analysis of 'evidence' images during content authoring.
sources.note: Auth: API key (AI Studio) or Google Cloud ADC (Vertex). Pricing (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing): Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite free tier input/output free; paid $0.30 in / $2.50 out per 1M. TERMS FLAG: free tier - 'Content used to improve our products': Yes; paid: No. Terms (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms): 'Google won't claim ownership over that content'; unpaid-service content may be read by human reviewers; users must be 18+. Free-tier RPM/TPM/RPD: not stated on docs page (shown in AI Studio).

sources.what: Official TypeScript client for the Mistral AI platform (chat, embeddings, OCR, moderation).
sources.use: EU-hosted budget NPC model; free moderation classifier to screen player-typed questions before they hit the main LLM.
sources.note: Auth: Bearer API key. Pricing (mistral.ai/pricing/api): Mistral Small 4 $0.15 in / $0.6 out per 1M tokens; 'Mistral Moderation 2' listed as Free. Free API tier/rate limits: not stated on the pages read (mistral.ai/pricing mentions '$10/mo in API credits' on a Free plan, unclear scope).

sources.what: Official Node/TS SDK for GroqCloud (low-latency LPU inference: chat, Whisper STT, TTS).
sources.use: Very low-latency NPC replies in voice mode; cheap Whisper transcription of player speech.
sources.note: Auth: Bearer API key. Pricing (console.groq.com/docs/models): GPT OSS 120B $0.15 in / $0.60 out per 1M; Whisper Large V3 Turbo $0.04 per hour; groq.com/pricing page did not render prices. Free plan limits (console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits): whisper-large-v3(-turbo) 20 RPM / 2K RPD; Orpheus TTS 10 RPM / 100 RPD / 1.2K TPM. Per-model LLM free limits vary.

sources.what: OpenRouter provider for the Vercel AI SDK - one key for hundreds of models (official SDK also at OpenRouterTeam/typescript-sdk, 254 stars, Apache-2.0).
sources.use: Plug into existing vercel/ai code to A/B NPC models or fall back across providers without new SDKs.
sources.note: Auth: Bearer API key. Pricing (openrouter.ai/pricing): free plan '25+ free models', '50 requests/day'; pay-as-you-go platform fee 5.5% (Standard) / 8% (Business); BYOK '$25,000 of list price inference / month with no fees, 5% fee after'. Limits (openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits): free models 20 RPM; 50/day if <$10 credits purchased, 1,000/day with >=$10. Output terms depend on the underlying provider.

sources.what: Official JS/Node SDK for the ElevenLabs API (TTS, voice design/cloning, STT, sound effects, music).
sources.use: Pre-render NPC voice lines (witnesses, pilots, 'official' spokespeople) and SFX in the asset pipeline; streaming TTS for live voice mode.
sources.note: Auth: xi-api-key. Pricing: elevenlabs.io/pricing - Free 10,000 credits/mo, no commercial licence; Starter $6/mo is cheapest with 'Commercial License, Instant Voice Cloning'. elevenlabs.io/pricing/api - Creator $11/mo incl. 220k chars TTS; $0.10 per 1K chars (v3/v2 Multilingual), $0.05 (Flash/Turbo); concurrency 4 (Starter) to 40 (Enterprise). TERMS (elevenlabs.io/use-policy): no replicating a person's voice 'without consent or legal right'; bans impersonating 'political candidates or elected government officials, regardless of whether authorization was obtained' - do NOT voice real UAP-hearing figures; use designed/fictional voices.

sources.what: ElevenLabs Agents SDK for TypeScript/React (conversational voice agents over WebRTC/WebSocket).
sources.use: Drop-in 'call the witness' voice-interview mode with a hosted agent and client-side React hook.
sources.note: Auth: agent ID (public agents) or server-minted signed URL/token. Pricing/limits: same account plans as elevenlabs-js (per-minute agent pricing not read). Same voice-cloning/impersonation policy applies. Vendor lock-in: agent config lives in ElevenLabs.

sources.what: Official JavaScript client for the Cartesia API (low-latency Sonic TTS, STT, voice cloning).
sources.use: Low-latency streaming TTS for real-time NPC voice replies.
sources.note: Auth: API key header. Pricing (cartesia.ai/pricing): Free 20K credits/mo, 2 concurrent TTS, NO commercial use; Pro $5/mo 100K credits (commercial); instant voice cloning on Free/Pro, professional cloning from Startup. Concurrency: Free 2 TTS, Pro 3, Startup 5, Scale 15.

sources.what: Official JS SDK for Deepgram (Nova STT streaming/batch, Aura TTS, Voice Agent API).
sources.use: Streaming STT for spoken player questions; Aura TTS as a cheaper voice option.
sources.note: Auth: API key / short-lived tokens for browser. Pricing (deepgram.com/pricing): '$200 free credit'; Nova-3 Monolingual streaming $0.0048/min (current, regularly $0.0077/min); Aura-1 TTS $0.0150/1k characters. PAYG concurrency: REST 50, WSS 150, TTS 45.

sources.what: Official JS SDK for AssemblyAI (async + streaming STT, audio intelligence, LLM gateway).
sources.use: Transcribe/diarize voice-mode sessions or recorded 'intercepts' for the asset pipeline.
sources.note: Auth: API key; temp tokens for browser streaming. Pricing (assemblyai.com/pricing): '$50 in free credits, no credit card required'; Universal-2 pre-recorded $0.15/hr, Universal-3.5 Pro $0.21/hr; Universal-Streaming $0.15/hr; streaming billed on session duration incl. idle. Limits: free 5 new streams/min, PAYG 100/min.

sources.what: LiveKit Agents (Python) - framework for realtime voice/video AI agents with STT/LLM/TTS plugins and turn detection.
sources.use: Host an interrogation-room voice agent (any STT/LLM/TTS mix) with barge-in; self-hostable.
sources.note: Auth: LiveKit API key/secret -> JWT access tokens. Pricing (livekit.com/pricing): Build (free, no card) 1,000 agent session min/mo, 5 concurrent agent sessions, 5,000 WebRTC min; Ship $50/mo 5,000 min, 20 concurrent. Page: agents framework and media server 'completely open source' and self-hostable - low lock-in.

sources.what: LiveKit Agents for Node.js/TypeScript.
sources.use: Same voice-agent worker as livekit/agents but in the project's TS stack (runs as a separate long-lived worker, not a Vercel function).
sources.note: Auth/pricing: as livekit/agents (livekit.com/pricing). Note: agents need a persistent process - deploy on LiveKit Cloud or a VM, not serverless.

sources.what: LiveKit browser client SDK (WebRTC rooms, audio tracks, data channels).
sources.use: Browser side of voice mode: mic capture and agent audio playback inside the three.js scene.
sources.note: Auth: server-minted JWT per player. Pricing: WebRTC minutes per livekit.com/pricing (5,000 free on Build).

sources.what: OpenAI Agents SDK for JS/TS - multi-agent workflows and realtime voice agents (browser WebRTC).
sources.use: Quick prototype of a realtime voice NPC using gpt-realtime with tool calls into case state.
sources.note: Auth: OpenAI API key; ephemeral client keys for browser realtime. Pricing: gpt-realtime-mini audio $10/$20 per 1M in/out (developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing). Lock-in: OpenAI-centric.

sources.what: Official Node.js client for Replicate (run hosted open models: image, video, audio, 3D).
sources.use: Asset pipeline: batch-generate concept art, texture variants, TripoSR/Hunyuan3D meshes without owning GPUs.
sources.note: Auth: Bearer API token. Pricing (replicate.com/pricing): no free tier mentioned; billed by hardware-time or per output, e.g. flux-dev '$0.025 / output image', A100 80GB '$0.001400 /sec'. Output rights follow each model's licence (check per model). Repo last pushed 2025-11 (slower maintenance).

sources.what: Official JS/TS client for fal.ai serverless generative media (queue, realtime, Next.js proxy).
sources.use: Fast image/video generation during content authoring; Next.js proxy route keeps key server-side.
sources.note: Auth: FAL_KEY (server) via bundled proxy. Pricing (fal.ai/pricing): output-based, e.g. Seedream V4 $0.03/image, Wan 2.5 $0.05/s video; H100 from $1.89/hr. Free credits: not stated. Per-model licence terms apply.

sources.what: Stability AI's official SDK (Python, legacy gRPC) for the Stability platform API; REST API is now primary.
sources.use: Pipeline-only: Stable Image Core/SD3.5 art and Stable Fast 3D meshes via REST (use fetch; SDK is Python/older).
sources.note: Auth: Bearer API key. Pricing: platform.stability.ai/pricing did not render; via search snippets of that page - 1 credit = $0.01, 25 free credits for new accounts, Stable Image Core $0.03, SD 3.5 Medium $0.035, Ultra $0.08 per image (unverified). Community License (stability.ai/license): free under $1M annual revenue; users own outputs; page covers self-hosted models, not API. SDK repo last pushed 2026-05.

sources.what: Official Tripo3D Python SDK (text/image-to-3D, texturing, rigging, format conversion).
sources.use: Pipeline script to generate prop GLBs (debris, artifacts, craft fragments) then optimize with glTF-Transform (in catalog).
sources.note: Auth: API key. Pricing (docs.tripo3d.ai/get-started/pricing.html): '$1.00 = 100 credits'; '300 free credits in 2 weeks'; text-to-3D 10 credits (H2/H3) or 30/40 (P1 untextured/textured); image-to-3D 20 or 40/50. Rate/concurrency limits: not stated. Output ownership: not stated on page read. Catalog already has TripoSR/TripoSG open models.

sources.what: Official Meshy 'agent-first' CLI (TypeScript) for the Meshy text/image-to-3D API (no official JS SDK found).
sources.use: Scriptable text-to-3D prop generation in the asset pipeline or from Claude Code.
sources.note: Auth: Meshy API key. Pricing (meshy.ai/pricing): Free 100 credits/mo, free-tier assets CC BY 4.0 (attribution, not owned); API access on Pro and above; Pro 1,000 credits/mo with 'private asset ownership' (price not captured). Very new repo (created 2026-08). Rate limits: not stated.

sources.what: Better Auth - framework-agnostic TypeScript auth library (sessions, OAuth, passkeys, orgs) stored in your own DB; now also stewards Auth.js.
sources.use: Player accounts / save-sync with your Neon/Turso/D1 DB; no per-MAU vendor fees.
sources.note: Auth model: self-hosted library, your DB. Cost (better-auth.com): OSS and free; optional paid 'Better Auth Infrastructure' dashboard (price not stated). Low lock-in. authjs.dev: 'The Auth.js project is now part of Better Auth.'

sources.what: Auth.js / NextAuth - OAuth/email/credentials auth for Next.js and other frameworks.
sources.use: Minimal Discord/GitHub OAuth sign-in (fits Discord ARG community) without a hosted auth vendor.
sources.note: Self-hosted, free. authjs.dev: 'The Auth.js project is now part of Better Auth' - consider Better Auth for new work. Repo last pushed 2026-07.

sources.what: Official Clerk JS monorepo (@clerk/nextjs, React components, backend SDK) for hosted auth.
sources.use: Fastest drop-in sign-in UI + user management for Next.js 16 if you accept a hosted vendor.
sources.note: Auth: publishable + secret keys; hosted user store. Pricing (clerk.com/pricing): Free 50,000 Monthly Retained Users per app; Pro $20/mo annual or $25/mo; $0.02/user for 50,001-100,000. LOCK-IN: user data and sessions live in Clerk.

sources.what: Isomorphic JS client for Supabase (Postgres via PostgREST, auth, storage, realtime, edge functions).
sources.use: All-in-one backend: auth + leaderboard tables + realtime presence for shared ARG puzzles.
sources.note: Auth: anon/service keys + RLS; Supabase Auth JWTs. Pricing (supabase.com/pricing): Free 50,000 MAU, 500 MB DB, 1 GB storage, 5 GB egress, 200 concurrent realtime conns, 2M realtime msgs/mo; 'Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity'; max 2 projects; Pro from $25/mo. Platform is OSS/self-hostable (moderate lock-in).

sources.what: Neon serverless Postgres driver (HTTP/WebSocket) for edge/serverless runtimes.
sources.use: Postgres for player progress, case state, leaderboards from Vercel functions (Vercel Marketplace integration).
sources.note: Auth: connection string. Pricing (neon.com/pricing): Free per project 100 CU-hours/mo, 0.5 GB storage, 5 GB egress, scale-to-zero after 5 min; Launch $0.106/CU-hour, $0.35/GB-month, 500 GB egress incl. Standard Postgres = low lock-in.

sources.what: HTTP-based Redis client for serverless/edge (Upstash).
sources.use: Leaderboards with sorted sets, session caches, daily-puzzle state from Vercel functions.
sources.note: Auth: REST URL + token. Pricing (upstash.com/pricing/redis): Free 500K commands/mo, 256 MB, 10 GB bandwidth; PAYG $0.2 per 100K commands, $0.25/GB storage. Note catalog has upstash/context7 (docs MCP), not these SDKs.

sources.what: Rate-limiting library for serverless runtimes on Upstash Redis (sliding window, token bucket).
sources.use: Protect LLM/TTS endpoints (NPC chat, hint API) from abuse and runaway spend per IP/user.
sources.note: Uses Upstash Redis quotas/pricing above (each check costs commands). No separate fee.

sources.what: TypeScript client for libSQL/Turso (edge-replicated SQLite, embedded replicas).
sources.use: Per-player or per-case SQLite DBs; cheap reads for evidence catalog queries.
sources.note: Auth: DB URL + auth token. Pricing (turso.tech/pricing): Free 100 databases, 5 GB, 500M rows read/mo, 10M rows written/mo; Developer $4.99/mo. SQLite-compatible (low lock-in).

sources.what: Wrangler CLI + Workers SDK monorepo (D1, R2, KV, Durable Objects bindings, Miniflare).
sources.use: Since the domain is on Cloudflare: R2 bucket for large 3D/audio assets (free egress), D1 for leaderboards, Workers for edge redirects.
sources.note: Auth: Cloudflare API token / wrangler login. D1 (developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/pricing): Free 5M rows read/day, 100,000 rows written/day, 5 GB; Paid 25B reads/mo incl + $0.001/M, 50M writes incl + $1.00/M. R2 (developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing): free 10 GB, 1M Class A, 10M Class B ops, free egress; $0.015/GB-mo. Catalog has cloudflare/mcp-server-cloudflare and partykit (not this).

sources.what: Official TypeScript library for the Cloudflare REST API.
sources.use: Call D1 over HTTP or manage R2/DNS/cache purges from Vercel-hosted code and CI.
sources.note: Auth: API token (scoped). Pricing: per product (see D1/R2 above). R2 is also S3-compatible, so any S3 SDK works (low lock-in).

sources.what: Vercel Storage SDKs monorepo (@vercel/blob, @vercel/edge-config).
sources.use: Store player-uploaded evidence/screenshots or generated audio; Edge Config for feature flags/case rotation.
sources.note: Auth: BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN; client uploads via signed tokens. Pricing (vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing): Hobby 1 GB/mo storage, first 10,000 simple ops, 2,000 advanced ops, 10 GB transfer - blocked (not billed) for 30 days if exceeded; Pro usage-based (example: $0.023/GB, $0.40/1M simple, $5.00/1M advanced ops). Rate limits Hobby 1,200 simple/900 advanced ops per min.

sources.what: UploadThing - typed file uploads for Next.js (server auth, client components).
sources.use: Player photo/'evidence' submissions for community ARG challenges.
sources.note: Auth: UPLOADTHING_TOKEN, auth checked in your route. Pricing (uploadthing.com/pricing): Free 2 GB storage, unlimited uploads/downloads; $10/mo 100 GB app; usage-based $25/mo 250 GB then $0.08/GB. LOCK-IN: hosted storage.

sources.what: Pusher Channels browser/Node client (server lib: pusher/pusher-http-node, 289 stars, MIT).
sources.use: Live 'disclosure event' broadcasts and shared puzzle presence without running a WebSocket server on Vercel.
sources.note: Auth: app key (client) + secret (server-signed private/presence channels). Pricing (pusher.com/channels/pricing): Sandbox free 200,000 msgs/day, 100 concurrent conns; Startup $49/mo 1M msgs/day, 500 conns. Proprietary protocol (lock-in). Catalog alternatives: partykit, liveblocks, colyseus.

sources.what: Official Ably JS/Node/React realtime pub/sub SDK (formerly ably-js).
sources.use: Realtime channels for global ARG events, presence, and message history.
sources.note: Auth: API key server-side, token auth for browsers. Pricing (ably.com/pricing): Free 6M msgs/mo, 200 concurrent conns/channels; Standard $29/mo + $2.50/M msgs, $1.00/M connection-min. Hosted (lock-in).

sources.what: Official Node.js library for the Stripe API (Checkout, Billing, webhooks).
sources.use: Sell the full game / supporter pack / physical dossier via Checkout; webhook unlocks entitlement.
sources.note: Auth: secret key + webhook signing secret. Pricing (stripe.com/pricing): 2.9% + 30c domestic cards; +1.5% international; +1% currency conversion; $15 dispute fee; no monthly fee. NOT merchant of record - you handle VAT/sales tax (Stripe Tax/Managed Payments price not captured).

sources.what: Official JS SDK for Lemon Squeezy (merchant-of-record store, licences, subscriptions).
sources.use: Sell game keys/licences with global tax handled; built-in licence-key API.
sources.note: Auth: API key + webhook secret. Pricing (lemonsqueezy.com/pricing): 5% + 50c per transaction, $0/mo; merchant of record (handles sales tax/VAT). FLAG: page shows 2026 notice 'Lemon Squeezy + Stripe Managed Payments' (platform transition - check roadmap); SDK repo last pushed 2024-11.

sources.what: Official Node.js SDK for Paddle Billing (server-side API + webhook verification).
sources.use: Merchant-of-record checkout for a paid PC/web release; handles global tax and fraud.
sources.note: Auth: API key + webhook secret. Pricing (paddle.com/pricing): 5% + $0.50 per checkout transaction; Paddle is MoR (tax/VAT, fraud, support); custom pricing for products under $10.

sources.what: Community object-oriented TypeScript wrapper for the Steam Web API (no LICENSE detected; no official Valve JS SDK).
sources.use: If a Steam release happens: read achievements/ownership/player summaries to sync with web leaderboards.
sources.note: Auth: Steam Web API key. Terms (steamcommunity.com/dev/apiterms): 'limited to one hundred thousand (100,000) calls to the Steam Web API per day'; key must stay confidential and is non-transferable. LICENCE FLAG: no licence on repo - get permission or call the HTTP API directly.

sources.what: discord.js - the main Node library for the Discord API (bots, slash commands, interactions).
sources.use: ARG community bot: drop timed clues, verify puzzle answers, assign 'clearance level' roles.
sources.note: Auth: bot token (gateway) / OAuth2. Discord API free. Limits (docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rate-limits): 'All bots can make up to 50 requests per second'; invalid-request limit '10,000 per 10 minutes' per IP. Needs a persistent process (not a Vercel function) or use HTTP interactions endpoint.

sources.what: butler - official itch.io CLI to push builds (channels, diff patching).
sources.use: CI step to publish the HTML5/desktop build of the game to itch.io on each release.
sources.note: Auth: API key or 'butler login' (itch.io/docs/butler). Free (itch.io revenue share not read). Not mandatory for HTML5 - itch app v26.12.0+ offers GUI uploads.

sources.what: React Email - unstyled React/TS email components, 60+ templates and preview editor (by Resend).
sources.use: Build 'classified dispatch' newsletter and case-update emails as React components, sent through the site's existing Resend setup.
sources.note: Free OSS library (react.email); works with Resend, SendGrid, AWS SES, Postmark, Nodemailer - no lock-in. Sending costs are Resend's (already in use).

sources.what: Resend's official Node.js SDK (the site already uses Resend).
sources.use: Send React Email templates, batch sends and audiences for ARG drops.
sources.note: Auth: API key. Pricing/limits: not read (existing vendor). LICENSE file is MIT.

sources.what: Novu - open-core notification infrastructure (workflows across email, in-app inbox, push, SMS, chat).
sources.use: In-game 'inbox' of incoming transmissions plus email/push fan-out from one workflow.
sources.note: Auth: API key; subscriber HMAC for Inbox. Pricing (novu.co/pricing): Free 10,000 workflow runs/mo; Pro from $30/mo; 'self-host the open-source Novu Project' free. LICENCE FLAG: GitHub NOASSERTION - open core (MIT core, enterprise features like SSO/audit logs under commercial licence per search results).

sources.what: web-push - Node library to send Web Push (VAPID) notifications; LICENSE file is MPL-2.0.
sources.use: Opt-in push alerts for new case drops / live events via the PWA service worker (catalog has serwist/workbox).
sources.note: Auth: self-generated VAPID keys; no vendor, free (browser push services deliver). Licence: MPL-2.0 per LICENSE (GitHub reports NOASSERTION) - file-level copyleft, fine as a dependency.

sources.what: Official Node.js library for the DeepL translation API (text, documents, glossaries).
sources.use: Pipeline translation of case files, NPC scripts and UI strings into next-intl/i18next message files with a glossary for in-world terms.
sources.note: Auth: DeepL-Auth-Key (Free keys end ':fx'). Pricing (deepl.com/en/pro-api): API Free 500,000 characters/month; API Pro base fee and per-character price not stated on pages read. TERMS: page says free-tier texts may be used for model improvement; Pro has data-privacy guarantees - use Pro for unreleased story content.

sources.what: LibreTranslate - self-hostable open-source machine translation API (Argos Translate models).
sources.use: Self-hosted fallback for translating player-submitted text/community content without per-character fees.
sources.note: Auth: optional API keys on your server. Hosted (portal.libretranslate.com): Pro $29/mo (80/min burst, 20/min sustained), Business $58/mo; 2,000 chars per call; self-hosting free. LICENCE FLAG: AGPL-3.0 - fine as a separate network service, but modifications served to users must be published.

sources.what: WASM port of Recast/Detour: navmesh generation, pathfinding, crowd simulation, three.js helpers
sources.use: Bake navmeshes for crash sites/bunkers so guards, recovery teams or creatures patrol and chase the player; DetourCrowd for group movement
sources.note: WASM payload adds download weight; bake navmesh offline and load the binary to keep mobile startup cheap

sources.what: Pure-JS navmesh construction and querying for 3D floor-based navigation (same author as recast-navigation-js)
sources.use: No-WASM alternative for NPC pathing in bunkers/labs; simpler to bundle with Next.js

sources.note: No licence and 0 stars. The source MoD files at The National Archives are Crown copyright, reusable under the Open Government Licence (check each file).

sources.what: Reproducible spatial point-pattern analysis of French GEIPAN UAP cases
sources.use: Shows how to load the official GEIPAN CSV (cases plus testimonies) and use its A/B/C/D classification as the 'explained vs unexplained' label
sources.note: MIT, 0 stars. Get the data from GEIPAN's official CSV download (cnes-geipan.fr), whose reuse terms are not clearly stated, so confirm with GEIPAN before redistributing.

sources.what: Scraper for GEIPAN case pages
sources.use: Fallback only. Prefer GEIPAN's official CSV exports
sources.note: Tiny, no licence. GEIPAN publishes CSV directly, so avoid scraping.

sources.what: Map data for UFO (and cryptid) sightings in Canada
sources.use: Only Canadian-specific data repo found. A possible seed for Canadian cases
sources.note: Unlicense code, 2 stars. The source of the sighting records is not verified, so check it before use. It may come from the Canadian UFO Survey (Ufology Research, Manitoba), which has its own terms.

sources.what: Global Meteor Network station software. GMN publishes daily meteor trajectory and orbit data
sources.use: Check whether a bright meteor was recorded near a sighting's time and place (the 'was it a meteor?' answer)
sources.note: The code is GPL-3.0 (tool only). GMN trajectory data at globalmeteornetwork.org/data is CC BY 4.0.

sources.what: Meteor physics library: trajectory solving, radiants, orbits, shower association
sources.use: Offline: rebuild a fireball's ground track from GMN or CNEOS data and assign it to a shower for the explanation reveal
sources.note: MIT.

sources.what: WebGL rendering of the debris streams behind meteor showers (CAMS data)
sources.use: Visual reference for an in-game 'why were there so many lights tonight' meteor-shower explainer
sources.note: MIT. Shower orbit data comes from CAMS/NASA, so check CAMS attribution.

sources.what: NASA CAMS meteor shower portal (SpaceML)
sources.use: Reference for showing CAMS meteor detections on a globe
sources.note: No licence (reference only). CAMS data is NASA/SETI-affiliated, so check the terms.

sources.what: Notebook that separates bolide signatures from lightning in GOES GLM data, using NASA's NEO-Bolide catalog
sources.use: Link a satellite-detected bolide (neo-bolide.ndc.nasa.gov) to a witness sighting
sources.note: Tiny (0 stars) but the only GLM-bolide repo. MIT. GLM data is NOAA open data (public domain).

sources.what: Tools for GOES-R Geostationary Lightning Mapper data (gridding, flash extraction)
sources.use: Rule lightning or bolide flashes in or out at a sighting location and time (2017 onward)
sources.note: BSD-3-Clause. GLM L2 data is NOAA open data on AWS (public domain).

sources.what: Client for live lightning strikes from Blitzortung.org
sources.use: Reference for live lightning overlays
sources.note: MIT code. Blitzortung data is for private, non-commercial use only and redistribution needs permission, so do not ship it in a commercial game. Prefer GLM or NOAA sources.

sources.what: Aurora forecasts and hindcasts from solar wind data (OVATION Prime 2010)
sources.use: Rebuild whether aurora was visible at a historic sighting's location (the 'was it the aurora?' explanation)
sources.note: LGPL-3.0: keep it offline or dynamically linked. Input solar wind data comes from NOAA/NASA (public domain).

sources.what: Byte-for-byte archive of NOAA SWPC OVATION aurora forecast snapshots, collected by GitHub Actions
sources.use: Historic aurora-probability grids for recent (2026+) cases. SWPC itself keeps only the latest
sources.note: Tiny (1 star, Sep 2026), no licence. NOAA SWPC data is public domain.

sources.what: Python wrapper for NOAA SWPC JSON services (Kp, solar wind, alerts)
sources.use: Fetch Kp and geomagnetic storm context for recent sightings
sources.note: Tiny (1 star), MIT. SWPC data is public domain. For historic Kp back to 1932 use GFZ Potsdam (CC BY 4.0).

sources.what: Open-source REST API and dataset of SpaceX launches, Starlink and landings
sources.use: Match 'strange spiral/plume' sightings to Falcon 9 launches and the Starlink batches deployed from them
sources.note: Apache-2.0, archived in 2024 so the data is frozen. Use Launch Library 2 for launches after that.

sources.what: MCP server for Launch Library 2
sources.use: Lets the authoring agent look up the launch that matches a sighting
sources.note: Tiny (0 stars), no licence. Free LL2 API tier is rate-limited (about 15 req/hr), so check TheSpaceDevs terms and cache responses.

sources.what: Launch statistics and charts built from the Launch Library 2 API
sources.use: Reference code for bulk-pulling and caching LL2 launch history
sources.note: Apache-2.0.

sources.what: Daily mirror of Jonathan McDowell's GCAT (General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects)
sources.use: Authoritative launch and reentry history since 1957 for 'was it a rocket or a reentry?' explanations
sources.note: Tiny mirror (1 star, NOASSERTION). The GCAT data is CC BY 4.0 (J. McDowell, planet4589.org), so attribute it. Prefer fetching from planet4589.org directly.

sources.what: 3D satellite tracker and pass predictor for 12,000+ CelesTrak satellites on a CesiumJS globe
sources.use: Reference for showing Starlink trains and ISS passes in the sky view
sources.note: MIT. Element sets come from CelesTrak (free use, attribute CelesTrak). Historical TLEs need Space-Track (account terms).

sources.what: Three.js/Svelte satellite tracker with sky view, visual magnitude and pass prediction
sources.use: Brightness estimates (visual magnitude) for 'bright moving light' Starlink/ISS explanations
sources.note: AGPL-3.0: tool only, never bundle.

sources.what: Python script that finds the brightest Starlink trains between astronomical twilight and sunrise
sources.use: Predict or hindcast whether a Starlink train was visible at a sighting
sources.note: Tiny (1 star) but the only Starlink-train predictor found. GPL-3.0: tool only.

sources.what: Python interface to SondeHub radiosonde telemetry (live and archived flights)
sources.use: Match 'silver balloon' sightings to real weather-balloon flights (2021 onward)
sources.note: GPL-3.0: tool only. SondeHub data is volunteer-collected, so check SondeHub's terms. Radiosondes are public NWS launches.

sources.what: Readers and utilities for NOAA's IGRA radiosonde archive
sources.use: Weather-balloon launch times and stations back to the 1940s, to test the balloon explanation for historic cases
sources.note: Tiny (1 star), no licence (reference only). IGRA v2 data is NOAA public domain.

sources.what: Daily open-data dumps of every aircraft trace seen by adsb.lol in 2026
sources.use: Check whether an aircraft was over a sighting location at that time (the 'was it a plane?' answer)
sources.note: The data is ODbL-1.0 (attribution and share-alike on derived databases). Very large, so sync none. It lists individual aircraft: never use it to look up people.

sources.what: 2025 archive of adsb.lol aircraft traces
sources.use: Same as 2026, for 2025 cases (includes the late-2024/2025 'drone wave' period)
sources.note: ODbL-1.0. Archived and very large.

sources.what: 2024 archive of adsb.lol aircraft traces
sources.use: Aircraft traffic for the Nov-Dec 2024 New Jersey 'drone' sightings, to test the plane explanation
sources.note: ODbL-1.0. Archived and very large.

sources.what: Nightly CSVs of worldwide airports, runways, navaids and frequencies
sources.use: 'Near an airport or approach path?' check for night-light sightings
sources.note: Public domain (Unlicense).

sources.what: Pattern detector built on FAA UAS (drone) Sighting Reports and public reports of incidents at military installations
sources.use: The only repo found that uses the FAA drone sighting reports. Seed for drone-explanation cases
sources.note: Tiny (0 stars), no licence (reference only). The FAA UAS Sighting Reports themselves are public US government records (faa.gov).

sources.what: Large QA dataset built on Chronicling America newspaper pages
sources.use: Example of large-scale access to ChronAm OCR text. Mine it for 1947 'flying disc' wave articles
sources.note: MIT code. Chronicling America pages are mostly public domain, but coverage now runs to 1963 and post-1929 pages may still be in copyright.

sources.what: Python client for the Chronicling America search API
sources.use: Search 1940s-1963 newspapers for 'flying saucer' reports by date and state
sources.note: No licence (reference; the API is simple enough to call directly). Chronicling America is moving to the loc.gov API.

sources.what: Script that exports Chronicling America search results to plain text and metadata
sources.use: Bulk-export the July 1947 flying-disc wave coverage for case writing
sources.note: GPL-3.0: tool only. Same ChronAm copyright caveat.

sources.what: MCP server for LOC digital collections and Chronicling America with full OCR text
sources.use: Lets the authoring agent search historic newspapers for contemporaneous accounts
sources.note: Apache-2.0.

sources.what: Original Chronicling America web app and API software (now superseded by Open ONI)
sources.use: Reference for the ChronAm data model (batches, OCR, METS/ALTO)
sources.note: Archived, no licence file (a US government work, likely public domain).

sources.what: LOC Tesseract pipeline that re-OCRs NDNP newspaper scans into ALTO XML and PDF
sources.use: Better OCR for faded 1940s-50s newspaper pages used as in-game clippings
sources.note: GitHub says NOASSERTION (a US government work). New in 2026.

sources.what: Code for the American Stories dataset: article-level text from Chronicling America scans, 1774-1963
sources.use: Article-level (not page-level) text of the 1947-1963 saucer waves, ready for search and clippings
sources.note: No repo licence. The dataset on Hugging Face is CC BY 4.0. Underlying newspaper copyright applies to post-1929 content.

sources.what: Code for the Newswire dataset of about 2.7M AP/UPI newswire articles from local papers, 1878-1977
sources.use: The best open source for the 1950s-1970s UFO waves (1952 Washington, 1966 Michigan 'swamp gas', 1973) as wire copy
sources.note: No repo licence. The dataset on Hugging Face is CC BY 4.0. Wire copyright may apply after 1929, so quote short excerpts.

sources.what: EffOCR: efficient character-level OCR for historical documents
sources.use: OCR low-quality scans of historic newspapers and typewritten memos
sources.note: Apache-2.0.

sources.what: Harvests Trove (National Library of Australia) newspaper search results with OCR text
sources.use: Australian UFO waves (e.g. 1954, Westall 1966, Valentich 1978 coverage)
sources.note: MIT. Needs a Trove API key. Trove API terms apply and articles after 1955 may be in copyright.

sources.what: Notebooks and examples for working with Trove digitised newspapers
sources.use: Recipes for date and place filtering of Australian coverage
sources.note: MIT.

sources.what: Python wrapper for the BnF Gallica APIs (French newspapers and documents)
sources.use: French press coverage of the 1954 French wave, to pair with GEIPAN cases
sources.note: AGPL-3.0: tool only. Gallica reuse is free for non-commercial use, but commercial reuse needs a BnF licence.

sources.what: Detects bad redactions (text still present under black boxes) in PDFs
sources.use: Game mechanic: let players 'x-ray' a redacted document. Also checks our own redacted props
sources.note: BSD-2-Clause. Only run it on public documents.

sources.what: DocumentCloud backend: OCR, entity extraction and annotation for document dumps
sources.use: Reference architecture for the in-game document viewer and OCR pipeline
sources.note: AGPL-3.0: reference or tool only.
